messages:
Incident Bot: Paging on-call — elevated 5xx rate from private VPC peering path to inference-gateway in us-west-2. Symptoms: gateway 502/504s, timeouts on internal health checks. Auto severity: P2. @Tu (oncall) tagged.

Tu (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing spike in 502s for customer-private-vpc prefix 10.20.0.0/16. Throttled flows to gw-proxy-az2. Starting live capture and collecting conntrack stats.

Maria G: Customer SRE reported errors at 09:12 UTC — most requests timeout after backend ACK. No recent deploys to gateway. Confirming which peering route table is used.

Raj P: I can pull NAT gw metrics — looks like SNAT table errors spiking; ephemeral port exhaustion-ish numbers, but ports still available. Also seeing a bunch of TCP RSTs from sg-priv-peering-1.

Charlotte H: Adding network-team. @Network Team can you check SG state sync between AZs? We had a control-plane resync earlier today.

Network Team: Acknowledged. Checking security group state across peering attachments. Seeing a mismatch: sg rules on transit appliance don't match the control-plane inventory for that peering - one side lacks the established flow allow for ephemeral return traffic. Could be state drift after migration.

Tu (oncall): That matches connection traces: many half-open connections and repeated SYN retransmits then RSTs. Dumping conntrack on nat-gw-03: ```sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.20. | wc -l -> 4231```

Maria G: Customer impact: ~12% of requests fail with 502/504 for that private tenant; some fall through to cached responses; others escalate to customer error pages. Notified Customer SRE.

Customer SRE: We're seeing errors on a small set of customers (org id: cust-8432) using Private deployment. They're routing inference calls through the peering path that looks affected. We're coordinating with their infra team.

Raj P: I see kernel logs on nat-gw-03: ```kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.``` But table size reported 65536/65536 — not growing beyond. Strange. Might be conntrack leak from asymmetric flows.

Tu (oncall): Quick mitigation idea: enable short-term connection tracking increase and aggressive conntrack GC on nat-gw-03, and add a temporary SG rule to allow established return traffic just for that peering. Will apply in canary then roll.

Charlotte H: +1 — propose canary in az2 only, so we can observe effect on error rate. Please annotate change in runbook and post the exact commands.

Tu (oncall): Applying canary now: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=100000``` and ```sudo sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal'``` then restarting conntrack helper GC. Also adding SG rule id sg-allow-return-temp (inbound) to peering-attachment-12 allowing established TCP from 10.20.0.0/16.  Applying in az2.

Ops Bot: Change recorded: sysctl update and SG rule sg-allow-return-temp created by Tu (oncall) at 09:21 UTC.

Network Team: Observing traffic post-change — conntrack table count drops to ~1200 for flows from that prefix, SYN retransmits reduce.

Maria G: Early metrics: 502 rate for that tenant down from 12% -> 3% in the canary AZ. Latency tail improving. Customer informed.

Customer SRE: Customer running live tests now. Confirming partial recovery; still seeing some errors on long-running streams.

Raj P: Long-running streams hit a secondary path via transit appliance in az1 which still shows drift. Need to apply same temporary SG rule to az1 nat-gw-05; also schedule a control-plane reconciliation for the peering.

Tu (oncall): Applying SG rule and the sysctl bump in az1 now. Rolling in az1.

Ops Bot: Change recorded: SG rule sg-allow-return-temp added to peering-attachment-11 at 09:34 UTC; sysctl updated on nat-gw-05.

Network Team: After az1 changes, drifted rules now in sync for the affected attachments. Suggest running a full reconciliation job (id: recon-2026-03-15-09) to surface remaining mismatches.

Maria G: Customer impact now reduced to <1% 502/504s across that tenant. Monitoring for 30m to validate. Will reopen if regression.

Tu (oncall): Leaving temporary SG rule in place and increased conntrack limit for next 4 hours. Plan follow-up: rollback sysctl to baseline after GC cools, then trigger full reconciliation and patch the control-plane bug that allowed SG drift. Filing follow-up ticket.

Charlotte H: Please create follow-up Jira and include runbook changes to detect SG state drift more proactively (add reconciliation alert when diff > 0.5% of peering attachments).

Tu (oncall): Created Jira INF-6721 "peering-sg-state-drift-root-cause-and-fix" and linked runbook edits. Tagging @Network Team for postmortem.

Incident Bot: Incident status updated to Mitigated at 09:49 UTC. Postmortem requested.

Maria G: Thanks team. I'll draft customer-facing summary and include timeline & mitigations.

Raj P: Adding kernel log excerpts and conntrack GC output to the postmortem.

Charlotte H: Handoff to day team: @Network Team take ownership for the reconciliation and RCA. On-call clear for now.

Network Team: Acknowledged. We'll run recon job, validate across both regions, and follow up with a PM for a permanent control-plane fix.

Tu (oncall): Marking thread resolved for oncall. If any regression, please ping immediately. :thumbsup:
